prompt: A factory's defect rate is $p = 0.10$. An inspector wants the sampling distribution of $\hat{p}$ to be approximately normal, which requires the Large Counts condition: $np \ge 10$ and $n(1-p) \ge 10$. What is the smallest sample size $n$ that satisfies both?
hint: With a small $p$, the harder condition to meet is $np \ge 10$ — you need enough expected defects.

hints.text: With a small $p$, the harder condition to meet is $np \ge 10$ — you need enough expected defects.

explanation: Normal approximation for $\hat{p}$ needs at least 10 expected successes and 10 expected failures.
Both must hold, so the binding one is $n \ge 100$. The smallest sample size is $100$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the condition exists
steps: With $n = 50$, you expect only 5 defects; the count is piled up near 0 and skewed right, not bell-shaped.
With 10 or more expected defects, the distribution has room to spread out symmetrically.
Ten expected defects at a $10\%$ rate means 100 items.
